---
title: "Session 2: Version control in RStudio"
subtitle: "Read repository state, review changes, and record meaningful checkpoints"
---

## Central question

Can you explain what changed, why it changed, and which version produced a result?

## Learning goals

By the end of the session, students should be able to:

1. Read file status in RStudio's Git pane.
2. Distinguish saved edits, staged changes, local commits, and pushed commits.
3. Clone the public course repository through RStudio.
4. Connect and verify a private `origin` using HTTPS browser authentication.
5. Invite the instructor and TA to the private repository for grading access.
6. Inspect line-level changes before staging their current versions.
7. Complete the everyday edit–review–stage–commit–push cycle through RStudio.
8. Use `.gitignore` appropriately.
9. Distinguish the student's private `origin` from the instructor's `upstream`.
10. Stop safely when a conflict, rejected push, or destructive choice appears.
11. Keep restricted data and credentials out of repositories.

## Materials

- [Before-class Git setup](preclass.qmd)
- [Interactive HTML lecture slides](slides.qmd)
- [Guided lab](lab.qmd)
- Lab starter: `course/session02/starter/` with `.Rmd` and `.qmd` report choices

The session teaches the RStudio interface first. The lab begins with a supervised
RStudio clone and the first authenticated private Push. Command-line equivalents
are provided as a reference, while the one-time remote setup and two-line course
update are supplied as copy-and-run recipes.
